description.value: A remote northern BC campground set amid old growth at the foot of the spectacular ~60 m Kinuseo Falls in Monkman Provincial Park, reached by roughly 65 km of gravel road from Tumbler Ridge — demanding on a loaded bike but one of the most dramatic waterfall camps in the province.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The OSM record identifies a 20-site campground within BC Parks' Monkman Provincial Park; the website is the official BC Parks page for that park and confirms it is active and open with camping as a listed activity. The website explicitly states a boil water advisory is in effect, providing direct negative evidence for potable water. OSM tags (power_supply=no, internet_access=no, sanitary_dump_station=no) offer supplementary signals but are not independently confirmed by the website text, so those amenities remain null per the rules.
concerns: OSM website URL points to the parent Monkman Park page rather than a dedicated Kinuseo Falls Campground page, limiting campground-specific amenity detail.
No phone number or physical address present in the OSM record.
Multiple subpages (contact, reservations, find-a-park) returned 404 errors, preventing verification of reservations and contact details.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Real, active BC Parks campground confirmed by official provincial parks website; a legitimate and notable destination for touring cyclists in northern BC.
enrichment_extras.notes: OSM tags indicate no power supply, no internet access, no sanitary dump station, and 20-site capacity; these are plausible for a remote BC Parks campground but could not be independently confirmed from the fetched website content.

wow_evidence: ~60 m Kinuseo Falls in Monkman Provincial Park... 65 km of gravel road
